hook: For fifty-four years, Real Madrid came to Greece and could not win.

beats.narration: For fifty-four years, Real Madrid came to Greece and could not win. Nine games. Six draws. Three defeats.
In Spain they had a word for it. Maleficio. A curse.

visual.headline: El Real Madrid no logra romper el maleficio griego

beats.narration: This is the story of every one of those nights. A European final in Piraeus. Three Athens clubs. Olympiacos, Panathinaikos, AEK.
From Madrid to Athens is a long way across the Mediterranean. Real Madrid have made the trip for finals, for group games, for nights they would rather forget.
And tonight, the fourth of November 2026, Real Madrid are back. At the new home of AEK.

visual.title: Tonight
visual.subtitle: AEK Athens v Real Madrid · 4 November 2026

beats.narration: It started with a final. Not even against a Greek club.
May 1971. The Cup Winners' Cup final, the first European final ever played in Greece. Real Madrid against Chelsea, at the Karaiskakis in Piraeus.
On the way they had beaten Hibernians of Malta, Wacker Innsbruck, Cardiff City and PSV Eindhoven.

visual.caption: Cup Winners' Cup · the road to the final

beats.narration: Miguel Muñoz's Madrid still had Gento and Amancio. Forty-two thousand watched.
Peter Osgood scored for Chelsea after fifty-six minutes. Madrid were going home with nothing.
Then, in the last minute, Zoco. One–one. Extra time, no winner.
There were no penalties in those days. The final was played again, forty-eight hours later, on the same pitch.
Dempsey and Osgood put Chelsea two up before half-time. Fleitas pulled one back. It was not enough.
Real Madrid's first two games in Greece. A draw and a defeat. The curse had its first page.
Fourteen years later, Madrid came back to Athens to play a Greek club for the first time.
September 1985. The UEFA Cup, first round. AEK Athens, at the Olympic Stadium. 39,819 inside.
Pavlos Papaioannou scored the only goal, with Márton Esterházy standing right in front of the Madrid goalkeeper. AEK one, Real Madrid nil.
Jacek Gmoch's AEK had given Real Madrid their first defeat at the hands of a Greek club, in Greece.
Madrid won the second leg five–nil, and went on to win the whole competition. But in Athens, they had lost.

visual.heading: The return leg in Madrid
visual.text: Real Madrid 5–0 AEK · Madrid went on to win the UEFA Cup

beats.narration: In the nineties, Olympiacos played their big European nights at the Olympic Stadium. Real Madrid came twice.
November 1997. Nil–nil. That season Madrid won their seventh European Cup.
September 1999. 70,800 people, and a goalkeeper of eighteen in the Madrid goal. Iker Casillas, eighteen years and a hundred and eighteen days.

visual.label: Iker Casillas, years old, in goal

beats.narration: Giovanni scored after eleven minutes. Sávio and Roberto Carlos turned it around before half-time.
Then Giovanni again. Then Zahović. Three–two Olympiacos.
And in the eightieth minute, Raúl. Three–three.
The Irish Times called him the saviour. Madrid won the Champions League again that season. Not in Athens.

visual.headline: Raul the saviour for Real Madrid

beats.narration: In 2002, two Athens clubs, seven months apart.
March. Panathinaikos at Leoforos, their old ground on Alexandras Avenue. Madrid had already won the group, and Del Bosque sent a young team.
Liberopoulos after nine minutes. Morientes two minutes later. Then Goumas, and Panathinaikos led again.
In the eightieth minute, a substitute in his first Champions League match. Javier Portillo. Two–two.
October. AEK, at the old Nikos Goumas in Nea Filadelfeia. Madrid brought Figo, Zidane, Raúl and Roberto Carlos.
After six minutes, Tsartas from a free kick. Zidane equalised. Then Maladenis and Nikolaidis, two headers in three minutes. AEK three, Madrid one.
Zidane again before half-time. Guti on the hour. Three–three.

The ground was not even full; tickets were expensive. The ones who came saw what Athens Voice later called perhaps the best match ever played in Greece. When Zidane came off, the whole ground applauded him.
Dušan Bajević had coached Olympiacos against Madrid in 1999. Now he was on the AEK bench.

visual.text: We came so near to making history.

beats.narration: Vicente del Bosque did not blame his defence.

visual.text: I would like to think all three goals were the result of AEK excellence rather than Madrid mistakes.

beats.narration: AEK drew all six of their group games that season. And in Spain, the morning papers wrote the word again. Maleficio.
In 2004 the Karaiskakis was rebuilt, and Olympiacos came home to Piraeus.
December 2005. Madrid had a new coach, Juan Ramón López Caro, in his first match. Sergio Ramos headed them in front after seven minutes.
Bulut equalised. And in the eighty-seventh minute, an old enemy from Barcelona. Rivaldo.
Olympiacos two, Real Madrid one.
Sky Sports had the headline that night.
November 2007, and Madrid were back. 33,500 inside. Van Nistelrooy hit the woodwork, so did Raúl. Nil–nil.
And in the Olympiacos defence that night stood Raúl Bravo, who had played for Real Madrid on the same pitch in 2005.
Then eighteen years without a visit.
November 2025. Karaiskakis again. Xabi Alonso against José Luis Mendilibar, the man who had won Olympiacos their European trophy.
After eight minutes, Chiquinho. One–nil Olympiacos. The curse was awake.
Then Kylian Mbappé. Twenty-two minutes. Twenty-four. Twenty-nine. A hat-trick in six minutes and forty-two seconds.
Taremi pulled one back. Mbappé scored his fourth on the hour. El Kaabi made it four–three in the eighty-first minute.
Four–three. Real Madrid's first win at Olympiacos, at the fifth attempt. Their first win in Greece.
Xabi Alonso said it plainly.

visual.text: We are back to winning ways, and we won in Greece for the first time.

beats.narration: Ten games in Greece. One win, six draws, three defeats.
Tonight, at 19:45 Athens time, the eleventh. Champions League, league phase, matchday four.
AEK's new ground stands where the Nikos Goumas stood, the ground of the three–three. It opened in 2022. Real Madrid have never played there.

visual.heading: AEK Arena · Nea Filadelfeia
visual.text: Built on the site of the Nikos Goumas · opened 2022 · Real Madrid’s first visit

beats.narration: José Mourinho on the Madrid bench. Marko Nikolić for AEK, champions of Greece for the fourteenth time. And up front for AEK, Luka Jović. A former Real Madrid striker.
Madrid have nine points from three games. AEK have three. On paper, there is no contest.
But in Athens, paper has never meant much. Ask Papaioannou. Ask Tsartas. Ask Rivaldo.
Fifty-four years of nights like these. Whoever you sing for tonight, you know why they matter.

description:
For fifty-four years Real Madrid came to Greece and could not win: a European final and its replay in Piraeus in 1971, then Olympiacos, Panathinaikos and AEK in Athens and Piraeus. Nine games, six draws, three defeats — the Spanish papers called it the Greek curse. In November 2025 Kylian Mbappé scored four at the Karaiskakis and it was over.

Tonight, 4 November 2026, Real Madrid play AEK Athens in the Champions League at the new AEK Arena, built where the Nikos Goumas stood — the ground of the 3–3 in 2002.

Every night, told from the stands: Zoco's last-minute goal in 1971, Papaioannou in 1985, Casillas at eighteen, Portillo's debut, Tsartas and Zidane, Rivaldo's winner, Raúl Bravo on both sides, and Mbappé's hat-trick in six minutes and forty-two seconds.

shorts.idea: The curse in numbers, then Mbappé's hat-trick in 6:42 and the 4–3.
